headline: South Asia: War in the Gulf
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: War in the Gulf.
- Western Russia: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.
- Africa: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
The United States-based software engineer accused of causing the leak of videos and photographs of a sexual encounter with a Jamaican attorney has lost a multimillion-dollar home in St Ann, which has been sold to settle a judgment handed down by the Supreme Court. Rodrick Brown, who resides in New York City, could possibly lose a second apartment as the attorney, Kimberley Facey, has filed documents in court seeking to recover millions of dollars in legal costs she incurred in pursuing the lawsuit against him.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.
Kärcher announced its Ukrainian warehouse was destroyed in a Russian strike on 27 September 2026, forcing the company to use alternative logistics.
- Ukrainska Pravda, just now: Russian drones attack cars in Kharkiv Oblast: two killed, two injured.
A 67-year-old man was killed when a Russian FPV drone struck a car in Shestakove, Kharkiv Oblast, while his wife suffered acute stress.
- The Moscow Times, 2 hours ago: Russia Hits Ukraine’s Largest Mobile Provider, Strikes Data Centers.
Kyivstar told Interfax Ukraine that its head office in Kyiv had been hit, but there were no casualties.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russians strike head office of Ukraine's mobile telecommunications operator.
A Russian drone strike damaged the Kyivstar head office on 27 September, as attacks continue targeting Ukraine's telecom and data centre infrastructure.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Five men arrested on terrorism offenses near UK airbase used for US strikes on Iran.
- Politico Europe, NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Five men arrested on terrorism offenses near UK airbase used for US strikes on Iran.
Britain authorized the U.S. to use the base for “defensive” strikes on Iran earlier this year.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market.
Seven people were killed and 40 injured in a Saudi airstrike on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, as Houthi forces advance and Saudi-led air raids intensify.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one hour ago: Sudan: RSF Drones Strike El Gezira Fuel Depot As Both Sides Report Shootdowns.
[Dabanga] Wad Madani -- Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces drones struck the Umm Alila fuel depot east of Wad Madani in El Gezira early on Sunday, triggering fires as Sudan's warring sides reported further drone activity across the country.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Nigerian foundation urges early screening in battle against childhood cancer.
The Okapi Cancer Foundation made the appeal during a childhood cancer awareness walk in Abuja, aimed at promoting awareness, mobilizing public participation, and raising resources for children battling cancer and their families
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one hour ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's Foretold War Arrives.
[African Arguments] No one can claim that a return to war in Tigray and northern Ethiopia is a surprise, but it makes it no less horrifying. In just a handful of days, and after months of spiralling tensions and sporadic fighting, the 'grey conflict' the federal government pursued against Tigray has escalated into ''full-blown war,' in the words of Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) vice president Ammanuel Assefa.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Trump: Indirect ceasefire talks between US, Iran to continue this week - report.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Trump: Indirect ceasefire talks between US, Iran to continue this week - report.
During a phone call with Axios, US President Donald Trump also said that he is “always thinking about” renewing strikes against Iran.
- Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: Mojtaba Khamenei injured before Iran war, pulled from Tehran hospital rubble after strike - report.
Ayatollah Mohsen Heidari Alekasir also denied the claim that Iran’s former supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, had recommended his son to serve as his successor.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Why Iran's new push for a deal to end the war appears to be stalling - analysis.
Iran proposed a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for a seven-day ceasefire, but the US seems uninterested as it wants something more to show from six months of conflict.
- Jerusalem Post, 8 hours ago: Israeli forces kill global jihadist terrorist who kidnapped Noa Argamani on October 7.
Later in the day, the IDF and Shin Bet announced that they killed Muhammad Hamad Muhammad Gabain, a commander in Hamas' military wing, who was involved in holding nine hostages abducted on October 7.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: War in the Gulf.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: War in the Gulf.
THE war that the US and Israel imposed on Iran this year has failed to achieve any of the objectives that the two countries had intended. The declared purpose was to prevent Iran from building a nuclear weapon. A fact-check indicates that Iran had kept its civil nuclear programme under IAEA safeguards. It had also willingly agreed to a nuclear deal in 2015. It was President Donald Trump who pulled the US out of the deal in 2018 and re-engaged with Iran in his second term under a “maximum pressure” campaign.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
- The Hindu - International, 11 hours ago: At least 7 dead as Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes and aerial war intensifies.
Russia has hammered Ukraine with missiles, glide bombs, and jet-powered drones, while frontline progress has slowed about 4.5 years after Moscow’s full-scale invasion
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Iran stands firm on Hormuz plan after US rejection.
Iran stood firm Sunday on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite United States President Donald Trump’s rejection of the proposal that had created some optimism for breaking the Mideast war stalemate. The waterway is key to the world’s energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.
Asia - bottom line: South African police probe mining feud shooting, 27 dead as elections near.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: South African police probe mining feud shooting, 27 dead as elections near.
South African police on Sunday were hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country’s problem with gun violence. Officials were still establishing the motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town, but initial investigations suggested one could be a turf war between illegal miners and the other a business rivalry. Afghanistan’s defence ministry said on Sunday its forces had killed 28 fighters and wounded 32 in the eastern province of Nuristan after a group it said included Islamic State militants travelled from Pakistan. The ministry alleged Pakistani militias ‌had supported the fighters and that most of them were former Afghan government security personnel. - Taipei Times, just now: Taiwan to build more anti-ship missiles.
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: How Beijing is neutralising Washington’s sanctions machine.
Last week, the president of the United States stood at the podium of the United Nations General Assembly and asked aloud whether he should “annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly”. Donald Trump then turned to Venezuela’s oil and declared: “To the victor belong the spoils, you’ve all heard that …” He spoke as the Iran war neared its eighth month, a week after the UN Human Rights Council found “reasonable grounds to believe” that the US had committed war crimes. India - bottom line: France steps in to protect Saudi oil infrastructure as Houthi attacks intensify.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: France steps in to protect Saudi oil infrastructure as Houthi attacks intensify.
France's military support to Saudi Arabia will involve deploying troops and defense systems to protect key energy infrastructure. The deployment follows repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and aims to secure the Red Sea port of Yanbu. French official Jean-Noel Barrot emphasized that France's role is strictly defensive and does not equate to participation in the conflict.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: LPU row escalates: Stones pelted, vehicles set on fire as police lathicharge students.
Students at Lovely Professional University protested against unverified claims of a rape on campus, leading to unrest. The protest intensified as students blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara National Highway, causing significant traffic disruption. Police attempted to resolve the situation but were met with stone-pelting from protesters, resulting in injuries on both sides.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: "View Was To Go With Palantir": Top Defence Official On "AI Spine" For Forces.
The top defence official revealed that "some attempts" to infuse AI were made during Operation Sindoor, India's counterstrike against terrorist havens in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: IndiGo A321 enroute Blr suffers tail strike; plane lands safely in second attempt.
On Sunday, an IndiGo Airbus A321 operating flight 6E 6542 experienced a tail strike during a go-around. The incident occurred while attempting to land in gusty weather at Bengaluru airport. All passengers and crew were safely disembarked, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and has engaged with IndiGo regarding pilot training enhancements.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: (LEAD) (Asiad) Swimmers lament decision not to award medals to relay heat participants.
- Yonhap News Agency, one day ago: (LEAD) (Asiad) Swimmers lament decision not to award medals to relay heat participants.
TOKYO, Sept. 26 (Yonhap) -- By taking bronze in the men's 200-meter butterfly at...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: UK police arrest five over alleged attack attempt on air base used by US.
- ABC News Australia, 8 hours ago: UK police arrest five over alleged attack attempt on air base used by US.
Five people have been arrested, UK police say, after a security scare at a British air base used by the US Air Force in south-west England since the start of the Iranian war.
